proof:
Source: parent Part III; valid for every P (including P = 0) and every open U (if U = ∅ all currents are 0). The final step uses part (1) of (IML), the third conjunct of sibling foundations, applied with (REP), (MR), (IMC). For a 0-covector α, ⟨α⟩ := α(∅).
1. H⁰ = μHE[0] = μH[0] is counting measure (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero, hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton). If (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep of S ∈ 𝒟_0(U), then M ∩ K is finite for compact K ⊆ U (θ ≥ 1, local integrability), the orientation condition holds at every point of M (no nonempty null sets), so ξ(x) = ε(x)⟨·⟩ with ε(x) = ±1, S(a) = Σ_{x∈M} m(x)⟨a(x)⟩ with m := εθ ∈ ℤ ∖ {0}, and by (MR) M_G(S) = Σ_{x∈M∩G}|m(x)| for open G.
2. For open W ⊂⊂ U, M_W(T) ≤ liminf_j M_W(T_j) < ∞ (WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf).
3. Fix x₀ ∈ U and r > 0 with B̄_{2r}(x₀) ⊆ U; c := sup_j M_{B_{2r}(x₀)}(T_j) < ∞. By step 1, for forms supported in B_{2r}(x₀), T_j(a) = Σ_{i≤N_j} ε_{j,i}⟨a(x_{j,i})⟩ with N_j ≤ c, ε_{j,i} = ±1, x_{j,i} ∈ B_{2r}(x₀).
4. Finitely many values of N_j and of the sign vectors and compactness of B̄_{2r}(x₀)^N give a subsequence with N_j = N, ε_{j,i} = ε_i and x_{j,i} → y_i.
5. For a with tsupport a ⊆ B_r(x₀): T(a) = lim_j T_j(a) = Σ_iε_i⟨a(y_i)⟩ = Σ_{y∈F} m(y)⟨a(y)⟩, where m(y) := Σ_{y_i=y}ε_i and F := {y ∈ B_r(x₀) : m(y) ≠ 0}.
6. (F, |m|, sign(m)⟨·⟩) is an IMRep in B_r(x₀) of T|_{B_r(x₀)}: F is finite (Borel, countably 0-rectifiable via constant maps), the fields are measurable, and since F is discrete the blow-ups of F at y ∈ F agree with {0} near the origin, so HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 F y {0}, oriented by ±⟨·⟩.
7. Steps 3–6 apply at every x₀ ∈ U; with step 2, part (1) of (IML) shows that T is IM. ∎
key_steps: Degree-0 IMReps are signed point sums.
Local point sums converge along a subsequence.
